title: Are zoos good or bad for animals?
summary: Josh and Chuck debate whether zoos are good or bad for animals. They open with banter about Ronnie Milsap and a chimpanzee masturbation anecdote, which leads to the term "zookosis" (coined by actor and animal rights activist Bill Travers) for repetitive, abnormal captive behaviors. The good side covers improved zoo conditions, captive breeding and reintroduction (California condor, Père David's deer), rescues (whale shark, snow leopard), better animal care (aardvark exhibit), conservation funding, and research. The bad side covers the USDA licensing of exhibitors versus AZA membership, weak conservation spending (about three percent of gate take), reintroduction success rates (16 of 146 in the twentieth century), elephant welfare and lifespan, escapes and animal deaths at US zoos (San Francisco Zoo tiger, Dallas Zoo gorilla, Virginia Zoo incidents), public education doubts, the Edith chimpanzee case, and the Luján-area zoo where visitors interact with predators. The episode ends with a Kiva team shout-out and T-shirt contest announcement; no listener mail.

segments.title: Opening banter and zookosis
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about Ronnie Milsap and then about chimpanzee self-abuse, leading to the term zookosis, which describes repetitive, abnormal behaviors in captive animals.

segments.title: Bill Travers and examples of zookosis
segments.summary: Bill Travers, an actor and animal rights activist, coined zookosis. Examples include pacing, overgrooming, self-mutilation, smearing feces, and regurgitation and reingestion among primates. Such behaviors are rarely seen in the wild.

segments.title: Case for zoos: improvements over time
segments.summary: The hosts agree zoos have improved, with larger habitats, moats replacing fences, and an end to procuring animals from the wild. Captive-born animals now make up many zoo populations.

segments.title: Conservation breeding successes
segments.summary: The California condor was brought back from fewer than two dozen birds through a captive breeding program run by the San Diego and Los Angeles zoos. Père David's deer went extinct in the wild and was reintroduced from captive stock.

segments.title: Rescues, animal care, and conservation funding
segments.summary: Zoos rescued animals from traveling circuses and poor conditions, including whale sharks moved to the Georgia Aquarium and a snow leopard sent to the Bronx Zoo. Animal care has improved, the Bronx Zoo opened a new aardvark exhibit, and zoos fund conservation projects, including Bronx Zoo spending in Africa.

segments.title: Research and the case for zoos
segments.summary: Zoos participated in about 2,030 research and conservation projects in more than eighty countries in 2002. Without zoo conservation, species such as the Père David's deer and California condor might be extinct.

segments.title: Case against zoos: licensing, conservation spending, reintroduction failures
segments.summary: Only about 200 of the roughly 2,400 US animal exhibitors belong to the AZA, which has stricter standards. Members spend about three percent of gate revenue on conservation. Of 146 reintroduction programs in the twentieth century, sixteen succeeded, and most were run by the US government.

segments.title: Elephants, escapes, and animal deaths
segments.summary: Elephants suffer in captivity; Detroit closed its elephant exhibit and Maggie the elephant in Alaska was confined in cold weather. Escapes and deaths include a Siberian tiger shot at the San Francisco Zoo, a gorilla shot at the Dallas Zoo, and incidents at the Virginia Zoo. African elephants in zoos live about 16.9 years versus 56 in the wild.

segments.title: Education, Edith, roadside zoos, and aquariums
segments.summary: Studies suggest visitors leave zoos less informed. The chimpanzee Edith was moved between facilities and ended in a filthy Texas roadside zoo. The hosts describe a Luján zoo where visitors ride lions, and discuss aquariums and killer whales. They end with a Kiva and T-shirt contest announcement, with no listener mail.
